claims.text: Virtual reality allows users to experience a sense of presence in a computer-generated three-dimensional environment.
Head-tracking devices alter displayed images naturally with head motion to enable immersion.
Virtual reality enables therapist-controlled delivery of sensory stimulation.

evidence.description: Virtual reality allows users to experience a sense of presence in a computer-generated, three-dimensional environment.
These devices track head movements so that the movements and images change in a natural way with head motion, allowing for a sense of immersion.
VR, which allows for controlled delivery of sensory stimulation via the therapist, is a convenient and cost-effective treatment.

methodologies.name: Systematic Literature Search
methodologies.description: A systematic literature review identifying studies implementing VR-based treatments for anxiety or other psychiatric disorders.
